issues.label: Jurisdiction on certiorari
issues.why: The court must confirm it has authority to review the ICA decision and the issues presented.

issues.label: Preservation of issues
issues.why: The court must determine whether the State’s arguments were properly preserved below and in the cert application.

issues.label: Proper standard of review
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standards for reviewing suppression rulings (fact findings vs legal conclusions) and ICA error.

issues.label: Kaneaiakala legal framework
issues.why: The court must correctly apply State v. Kaneaiakala’s due process/reliability test for eyewitness identifications.

issues.label: Step-one suggestiveness
issues.why: The court must decide whether the show-up procedure was impermissibly suggestive under the totality of circumstances.

issues.label: Step-two reliability
issues.why: Even if suggestive, the court must decide whether the identification was nevertheless sufficiently reliable to admit.

issues.label: Totality-of-circumstances scope
issues.why: The court must decide what circumstances must be considered (system variables, estimator variables, and case-specific facts).

issues.label: HAWJIC 3.19 role
issues.why: The court must decide how the 3.19 factors inform reliability and whether the circuit court adequately considered them.

issues.label: HAWJIC 3.19A role
issues.why: The court must decide whether 3.19A factors must be expressly addressed in admissibility rulings or are merely guidance.

issues.label: Need for express findings
issues.why: The court must determine whether the trial court must make explicit findings on each factor or whether implicit consideration suffices.

issues.label: Adequacy of trial court findings
issues.why: The court must assess whether the circuit court’s stated reasoning demonstrates consideration of relevant suggestiveness/reliability factors.

issues.label: Police said suspect in custody
issues.why: The court must weigh the suggestive impact of telling CW police had a male in custody before the show-up.

issues.label: No may-or-may-not warning
issues.why: The court must evaluate the effect of failing to warn CW the perpetrator may not be present, especially due to language barrier.

issues.label: Single-person show-up
issues.why: The court must consider the inherent suggestiveness of presenting one handcuffed suspect alone to the witness.

issues.label: Handcuffs and officer presence
issues.why: The court must assess whether visible custody cues (handcuffs, officer behind) increased suggestiveness and tainted reliability.

issues.label: Ambulance reroute to show-up
issues.why: The court must consider whether transporting CW to view the detained suspect created pressure to identify.

issues.label: Witness condition and stress
issues.why: The court must consider CW’s age, injury, medical distress, and stress effects on perception and memory.

issues.label: Opportunity to observe attacker
issues.why: The court must evaluate CW’s viewing conditions during the assault (duration, distance, lighting, focus) bearing on reliability.

issues.label: Prior familiarity absent
issues.why: The court must account for CW having no prior contacts with the assailant, affecting identification confidence/reliability.

issues.label: Time between event and ID
issues.why: The court must weigh the short time lapse between assault and show-up as a reliability factor.

issues.label: Accuracy of initial description
issues.why: The court must consider CW’s ability to give a description and how well Jercy matched it.

issues.label: Description filtered by interpreter
issues.why: The court must assess reliability of the description/communications given they were mediated by granddaughter and language limitations.

issues.label: Interpreter absence at show-up
issues.why: The court must consider whether lack of Chuukese interpretation prevented proper instructions and affected fairness/reliability.

issues.label: Cross-racial identification
issues.why: The court must consider whether cross-racial/ethnic factors were present and how they affect identification accuracy.

issues.label: Witness certainty evaluation
issues.why: The court must consider CW’s expressed certainty and whether it was influenced by suggestive procedure.

issues.label: Memory contamination risk
issues.why: The court must consider whether the suggestive show-up could have altered CW’s memory for later in-court ID.

issues.label: Independent source for in-court ID
issues.why: If the show-up was improper, the court must decide whether any in-court identification had an independent basis.

issues.label: Suppression remedy scope
issues.why: The court must determine whether suppression should exclude only the show-up ID or also subsequent identifications/testimony.

issues.label: Burden of proof at suppression
issues.why: The court must ensure the correct party bears the burden under Kaneaiakala to prove admissibility/reliability.

issues.label: Constitutional basis
issues.why: The court must determine whether analysis rests on Hawaiʻi due process, federal due process, or both, and any divergent protections.

issues.label: ICA’s legal-error premise
issues.why: The court must decide whether the ICA correctly held the circuit court failed to consider 3.19A and suggestiveness effects.

issues.label: ICA requirement of explicit 3.19A
issues.why: The court must resolve whether ICA improperly imposed a requirement to expressly address each 3.19A factor.

issues.label: Whether circuit court did consider suggestiveness
issues.why: The court must determine if the record shows the circuit court considered the key suggestiveness facts despite not citing 3.19A.

issues.label: Focus on reliability vs suggestiveness
issues.why: The court must clarify that the dispositive question is reliability notwithstanding suggestiveness and whether ICA misapplied that focus.

issues.label: Harmless error standard
issues.why: If error occurred, the court must apply the correct harmless-beyond-a-reasonable-doubt standard for constitutional identification error.

issues.label: Prejudice assessment on record
issues.why: The court must evaluate the strength of other evidence of identity absent the show-up to determine harmlessness.

issues.label: Other eyewitness reliability
issues.why: The court must consider limitations in neighbor identifications/chase gaps and their effect on harmlessness and overall proof.

issues.label: Sufficiency of identity evidence
issues.why: The court must ensure the remaining evidence, if identification suppressed, is sufficient to support conviction or requires acquittal/new trial.

issues.label: Proper appellate remedy
issues.why: The court must decide whether to affirm, reverse, remand for new suppression findings, or order a new trial with/without ID evidence.

issues.label: Scope of remand instructions
issues.why: If remanding, the court must specify whether the circuit court must conduct a new Kaneaiakala hearing and make detailed findings.

issues.label: Impact on jury instructions
issues.why: The court must consider whether HAWJIC 3.19/3.19A were given and whether any instructional error affects the conviction.

issues.label: Standard for show-up permissibility
issues.why: The court must consider whether exigency/necessity justified a show-up rather than lineup and how that bears on due process analysis.
